title: Whole Orchard Tree Picker and Basket Margin
description: One static orchard-edge collection-preparation display scene, zero new models. One entire qualified forked-trunk orchard tree stands at the left rear, while an entire qualified upright high side-cup fruit picker is parked separately to its right and one entire qualified empty coarse-band harvest basket occupies a distinct front-right station. All three originals preserve every oriented world triangle, full unit-scale dimensions and opaque per-face PBR. The picker does not touch the tree or reach into the crown, and there is a real open foreground strip; no fruit is added or retained. One finite scene-only earthy floor is the only new mesh. The unchanged tree root tips and low trunk are intentionally embedded 35mm into that ground, with selected actual finite material overlap; the complete picker pole sole and basket base rest on the top plane. This is not the old stone-trough/firewood-shelter workyard or the poultry apparatus court with renamed equipment: its whole tall tree edge, independent upright collection tool and low empty receiving position form a new visual relationship. Source hierarchy is baked and normals recomputed, not original GLB byte retention; whole translated coordinates are explicitly stored float32. No growth, fruit collection, basket capacity, tool-to-tree reach compatibility, pole stability, access, ecology, working procedure, loading or safety validation. Rig animation and interaction not made.
